title: Andreeva Fights Back to Beat Sabalenka
summary:
Mirra Andreeva was losing badly. Then she turned the match around.

The 19-year-old from Russia was 4-1 down in the first set against Aryna Sabalenka, the world number two, at the WTA Finals. But Andreeva found her best tennis and never let go. She won 11 games in a row and took the match 6-4, 6-0. The win sent her into the last four.

Andreeva mixed high, looping balls with strong shots from the back of the court. She hit 16 winners and made only six mistakes. When she served for the first set at 15-30 down, she hit three aces in a row.

Sabalenka started well and led by two breaks. But after that she won only 10 more points in the whole match, and she finished with 23 mistakes.

Andreeva said afterwards that Sabalenka did not have her best day, and that she was happy. Andreeva now goes through as the winner of her group. Sabalenka can still reach the last four if she beats Elina Svitolina on Friday.
why_it_matters: It shows that a game is never over until the last point, so keeping going when you are losing can turn things around.

The WTA Finals is a big end-of-season event where the best women players face each other in groups, and the top players move on to the last four.
A player who is losing can still fight back by changing how she hits the ball, as Andreeva did with high, looping shots and strong hits from the back of the court.
